B-NSC.why: On the date of death he was receiving VA disability compensation, so the non-service-connected burial allowance is owed (38 CFR 3.1705(b)): the actual cost up to $978 for a death from 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2025, and the funeral cost $9,465. VA must receive it no later than 2 years after his burial on 11 October 2024 (3.1703(a)(1)): by 11 October 2026, two days away

B-PLOT.why: Buried in a private cemetery, not a national one, and eligible for the non-service-connected allowance, so the plot or interment allowance is owed to the person who paid (3.1707(c)): the lesser of $978 and the $2,150 for the lot and interment, with nothing paid by a State, the United States or an employer (3.1711(a)). No time limit

traps.B-SC: His death was not service-connected: the cause was pancreatic cancer, no rated condition, and the presumption for a veteran rated totally disabled does not reach a total rating that rests on individual unemployability (3.1704(b)). Claiming $2,000 would claim a service-connected death the record contradicts
traps.B-HOSP: He died at home under a private hospice, not hospitalized by VA or in care it paid for (3.1706): the allowance he is owed is B-NSC

B-TRANS.why: 3.1709(b) pays the reasonable cost of transporting the remains to the place of burial for a veteran receiving compensation; the $395 transfer and $350 hearse may qualify on an itemized statement, a judgement VA makes. Harmless either way

M-3.why: VA furnishes a marker for the unmarked grave of an eligible veteran in a private cemetery at no cost (38 CFR 38.630), and Cedar Hollow's Section D allows only flat bronze markers: the government flat bronze marker, worth the $1,240 Wrenfield charges for the same marker; the $225 setting fee stays the family's

traps.M-1: Section D allows no upright headstones: the cemetery would not certify placement
traps.M-2: Section D allows no upright headstones: the cemetery would not certify placement
traps.M-4: Section D allows only bronze markers, not granite
traps.M-5: Section D allows only bronze markers, not marble
traps.M-6: A medallion is for a grave already marked with a privately purchased headstone; his grave has only a temporary marker

traps.WM-1: VA furnishes the same flat bronze marker at no cost: buying it from the funeral home pays $1,240 for nothing
traps.WM-2: An upright headstone is not allowed in Section D, and VA would furnish a marker free
traps.WM-3: A plaque for an existing headstone, and the grave has none

traps.BL-1: No fee may be charged for preparing or filing an initial VA claim, and only accredited agents may charge at all (38 CFR 14.636(b), (c)): the claim is free to file

BL-2.why: Daniel's own electricity bill: paying it is his business, not this chore
